📰 General

Sarkozy’s Corruption Conviction Upheld by French Court in Landmark Ruling •

The French Court of Cassation has affirmed a previous conviction against former President Nicolas Sarkozy for illegally funding his 2012 presidential campaign. The court determined that Sarkozy significantly exceeded France’s electoral spending restrictions, a violation of campaign finance laws. This ruling stems from an investigation into the “Pegasus” affair, involving the alleged illegal channeling of campaign funds. The Court of Cassation’s decision effectively ends Sarkozy’s appeal, solidifying the original conviction.

🌍 World

EU Agrees on Landmark Law to Combat Online Child Sexual Abuse •

The European Union reached a provisional agreement on Wednesday to implement new legislation aimed at combating online child sexual abuse. This agreement concludes a protracted lobbying battle involving various European governments and privacy advocacy groups. The proposed law will require online platforms to proactively identify and remove content exploiting or endangering children. It mandates enhanced reporting mechanisms and increased cooperation between law enforcement and tech companies to address this growing issue. The legislation is expected to be formally adopted by the European Parliament in the coming weeks.

🦅 US

Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy Ruled Out for Sunday’s Game Against the Seahawks •

The Minnesota Vikings have not ruled out J.J. McCarthy from appearing in Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks. However, multiple team sources indicate the young quarterback is unlikely to play due to an undisclosed injury. Undrafted rookie Max Brosmer is slated to start at quarterback for the Vikings. The team has not disclosed the nature of McCarthy’s injury or the extent of his recovery. This decision leaves the Vikings with an uncertain quarterback situation heading into the matchup.

💰 Business

Surveillance Footage Reveals New Angles in UPS Plane Crash Investigation •

Newly released surveillance video from the Louisville Regional Airport Authority offers previously unseen perspectives of the November 4th crash of Flight 2976. The footage, captured from jet bridges, provides detailed views of the aircraft’s trajectory leading up to the incident. Authorities are utilizing this expanded visual data to aid in the ongoing investigation into the cause of the crash. The video represents a significant addition to the evidence collected by investigators.

💻 Technology

Black Friday 2025: Sony Offers $20 Discounts on All PS5 DualSense Controllers •

Sony is offering significant discounts on all PlayStation 5 DualSense controllers as part of its Black Friday 2025 sale. The company has reduced the price of every available color by $20, including previously unavailable limited edition models. This represents a notable price drop for consumers seeking to upgrade their gaming experience with the popular controller. The sale is currently active and offers a limited-time opportunity to purchase the DualSense at a reduced cost.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya graced the 2024 Met Gala with a breathtaking custom Valentino Haute Couture gown designed by Pierpaolo Piccioli. The dress featured a dramatic, floor-length silhouette with intricate embellishments and a deep V-neckline. She accessorized with Tiffany & Co. jewelry and a stunning diamond bracelet. The event celebrated the theme "Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion," and Zendaya’s appearance was widely considered a highlight.

🏅 Sports

Patriots Place Rookie Left Tackle Will Campbell on Injured Reserve •

The New England Patriots have placed rookie left tackle Will Campbell on the injured reserve. The decision follows a knee injury sustained by Campbell during last Sunday’s victory. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced the placement at Wednesday’s press conference. Campbell is expected to miss at least the next four games while he recovers. The team has not yet specified the severity of the injury.

🔬 Science

Ancient Foot Fossil Reveals New Human Relative Alongside “Lucy” in Africa •

Scientists have identified the owner of a 3-million-year-old foot fossil discovered in Ethiopia as a previously unknown ancient human relative. The fossil, unearthed in the Afar region, belongs to a species recently named alongside Australopithecus afarensis, the species to which “Lucy” belonged. Analysis of the bone structure suggests this new species coexisted with Lucy in Africa approximately 3 million years ago. Researchers believe this discovery provides further insight into the diversity of hominin populations during the Pliocene epoch.

🩺 Health

Blood Pressure Supplement Shows Promise in Clearing Alzheimer's Signs in Mice •

Researchers have identified a supplement commonly used to treat high blood pressure that appears to reduce the accumulation of harmful proteins associated with Alzheimer’s disease. The study, conducted on mice, demonstrated that the supplement successfully cleared sticky protein build-ups in the brain, a key characteristic of the disease. Furthermore, the effect was also observed in fruit flies, suggesting a potential mechanism of action. Scientists are now investigating whether this supplement could be a viable treatment option for humans with Alzheimer’s.
